summary:
Travelers to Pennsylvania stand under the United States federal framework. Executive Order 14168 of January 2025 redefined sex for federal purposes as a male-female binary, barred transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with their gender identity, and prohibited self-selection of gender on passports and visas. The State Department has stopped processing the X marker and issues passports only as M or F according to supporting documents; passports already carrying X remain valid until expiry. The Supreme Court allowed the passport sex-marker restrictions to take effect in November 2025, and the ACLU is suing the State Department on behalf of seven plaintiffs over the changed treatment of trans passport applicants.

Executive Order 14201 of 5 February 2025 and a State Department announcement of 25 February 2025 bar visas for trans athletes entering the country to compete in women's sporting events; applicants are flagged under an internal marking, and a declared gender other than sex assigned at birth may be treated as fraud carrying a permanent bar. Screening at checkpoints carries an outing risk through secondary screening, devices and pat-downs, and several foreign governments, including at least eight European states, adjusted travel guidance for trans and nonbinary citizens entering the country during 2025.

Pennsylvania itself sits in the low-risk tier of Erin Reed's anti-trans national legal risk assessment as updated in July 2026, which covers states that largely refrain from targeting trans adults without specially protecting them, while documenting continued national degradation of trans rights through the 2026 legislative season.

The live legislative risk in Pennsylvania concerns school and collegiate athletics rather than adult status, documents or public facilities. The Pennsylvania Senate passed Senate Bill 1293, the Save Women's Sports Act, on 22 April 2026, which would ban transgender female athletes from girls' and women's teams in the commonwealth; Governor Josh Shapiro called supportive lawmakers 'extremists', and it was unclear whether the House of Representatives would take the bill up. The Senate had already approved Senate Bill 9 on 6 May 2025, reserving women's-designated teams for 'biological females' in K-12 and collegiate sports and sending it to the House.

Pennsylvania has also declined an anti-trans measure of this kind: Governor Tom Wolf vetoed comparable legislation on 11 July 2022 that would have required public K-12 schools and colleges to designate sports as male, female or coed, with female-designated sports limited to athletes assigned female at birth. Both pending bills target youth sports participation rather than transgender adults or public-facility access, so a trans visitor to Pennsylvania faces no state-level restriction on restroom use, identity documents or medical care under the sources available here.
tangentialFactors:
The federal layer around Pennsylvania is markedly harsher than the state layer. A July 2026 national risk assessment flagged Idaho as the fourth state labelled 'Do Not Travel' for trans people, and state document rules tightened elsewhere, with Kansas enacting a law in February 2026 barring marker changes on birth certificates and driver's licences and invalidating existing non-matching documents.

Facilities restrictions are concentrated outside Pennsylvania. A Movement Advancement Project tally counts state bathroom bans applying to trans people in K-12 schools and some government buildings in nine states and one territory, with outright state bans on facility use per gender identity in additional states, while 29 states, four territories and the District of Columbia have no such ban. In April 2025 a transgender student was arrested and handcuffed in a women's restroom at the Florida state capitol, described by civil-rights attorneys as the first known arrest under that state's bathroom-restriction law.

Gender-affirming care for children is banned in 27 states nationally, and federal measures including Executive Order 14187 and October 2025 Medicaid proposals have been blocked or enjoined in court in part. Federal custody practices, including conversion-therapy-style policies adopted by the Federal Bureau of Prisons from 2026 and cash bounties directed at trans activists from December 2025, apply nationwide regardless of state law.

Pennsylvania's trajectory runs against its neighbours in one respect: the state Senate's repeated approval of athletic restrictions in 2025 and 2026 has been met with executive opposition rather than enactment, whereas comparable measures have been signed into law in a number of other states.
localsOnly:
Pennsylvania residents who are students or athletes are the population directly affected by the two Save Women's Sports Act measures. Senate Bill 9, approved 6 May 2025 with sponsors including Senators Judy Ward and Kristin Phillips-Hill, would reserve women's-designated teams in the commonwealth's K-12 and collegiate sports for 'biological females'; Senate Bill 1293, passed 22 April 2026, would bar transgender female athletes from girls' and women's teams. Neither bill has been shown in these sources to have been enacted or to have cleared the House of Representatives.

Executive opposition is on the record. Governor Tom Wolf vetoed the 2022 version of the sports restriction on 11 July 2022 after it passed the Republican-led legislature largely on party lines, and Governor Josh Shapiro publicly characterised lawmakers supporting Senate Bill 1293 as 'extremists'. The measures as written concern youth school sports and do not reach transgender adults' access to public facilities, identity documents or medical care.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Senate Bill 1293 or Senate Bill 9 advances beyond the Pennsylvania Senate is unresolved in the sources; the House of Representatives' intent was reported as unclear as of April 2026, and no later status is sourced.

The sources available here do not address Pennsylvania rules on birth certificates or driver's licence sex markers, state-level hate-crime coverage of anti-trans offences, or state recognition of identity documents and partnerships. Any such provisions are not sourced rather than absent.

Which federal measures remain blocked or enjoined at the time of a visit is unresolved; the parent framework notes that several federal actions have been challenged in court without specifying their current status. Enforcement practice at Pennsylvania airports and federal facilities, including TSA screening and any local law-enforcement response, is not documented in this inventory.
